back: The study of past human activities and events, based on evidence.
A source produced at the time of the events or by a participant or witness.
notes: Examples: a diary, a treaty, a photograph, a tool from a site.

back: A source produced later by someone who was not there, usually from primary sources.
Knowledge of the past passed down by word of mouth: stories, praise poetry, songs, proverbs and genealogies.
The study of the human past through material remains such as tools, pottery, bones and buildings, often found by excavation.

front: Name the five main kinds of historical source.
back: Archaeology and artefacts; written documents; oral tradition; pictures and photographs; buildings and sites.

front: Give one strength and one weakness of oral tradition.
back: Strength: preserves African points of view and the history of societies without writing. Weakness: details and dates may change as it is retold.

front: Why must early written documents about Zimbabwe be used with care?
back: Most were written by outsiders (traders, missionaries, officials) who often misunderstood African societies or wrote to serve their own interests.
Political, economic, social, local and family history.
Each source has weaknesses; when independent kinds of source agree, a conclusion is more reliable.
